full_judgment:
7. Mr Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, the learned counsel appearing for the defendant No. 2- appellants upon taking us to the impugned judgment as well as other documents so appeared in the paper book at the very outset submits that, admittedly the suit land has been recorded in the name of Hira Lal Agorwala in SA khatian and though the learned Joint District Judge has not touched upon the very vital question giving any observation as to what prevented the plaintiff in recording his name in the SA khatian in spite of the fact that, his predecessor took settlement of the suit land by virtue of amalnama in the year 1953 AD and thereby erred in law in decreing the suit. 

 17. In contrast, Mr Md Nurul Amin, the learned senior counsel along with Mr SM Tariqul Islam, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent No, 1(a)-1(g) very robustly opposes the contention so have been taken by the learned counsel for the appellants and contends that, mere recording the name of the predecessor of the present appellants in the SA khatian does not ipso facto confer/create right, title and ownership of the present appellants in the suit property because it has been settled as soon as invasion over title is made, then the aggrieved party can bring a suit and hence in the instant suit, the plaintiff was not required to challenge the preparation of the latest record though stands in the name of the predecessor of the defendant No. 2-appellants, Hira Lal Agorwala.
